_doc: Where the STAND-IN's face was marked, in pixels of the crop `crop_px` of the copy named in `scan` (T-3553; the owner: "their faces must match exactly"). The `mp_<index>` marks are MediaPipe Face Landmarker's (float16 v1) points on the owner's picture, every one the correspondence table (data/humans/variation/mediapipe_hm08_landmarks.json) puts on a skin vertex, and the face's outline ring (`mpo_<index>`) on the vertices it falls on in the calibration render turned as the portrait is (`outline_yaw_deg`, the yaw of a first fit without it), at 8 px where the forehead's edge is under the hair; they were checked by eye on a 3x enlargement. The pupils are the model's iris centres; the ears were read by eye on a gridded enlargement. `prior_widen` 2 lets this many points hold the face instead of the town's average. She sits turned a little to her right; her right ear is in shadow under the hair, so only its lobe (where the hoop hangs) is marked. `base_body` fits against the lady's body's rest face. The 18 outline marks below the nose were then moved once by what a render of the fitted face, turned as the portrait is and read by the same landmark model, put off them (up to 6 px; the render's chin sat about 5 px to her left and its jaw a little wide), so the next fit lands the drawn outline where the picture's is (T-3553, 2026-11-13). The lips' marks were moved the same way, once (T-3553, 2026-11-13, the owner: match her lips better): the render drew her lower lip's lower edge several pixels below the picture's.
age_note: The picture is undated and its sitter unnamed; the sitter looks about 45. The owner gave it as Sarah Grey's likeness for 1904, when Sarah was 54 (1900 census). The face is fitted as a face of 45, and the figure is drawn at that age (`likeness.drawn_age`), so the town shows the portrait's face rather than one aged 9 years past it; the person's record keeps 54.
basis: No photograph of Sarah Grey is known. The owner supplied this sepia cabinet-style portrait on 2026-11-12 as the likeness to use for her in 1904 ("since we do not have photos of them you can use these likenesses"). Who sat for it and when it was made are not recorded, so it is a stand-in: her face's proportions, hair and dress follow it, and none of it is evidence of how Sarah Grey looked.
not_modelled: her own face (no photograph of her is known; this is the owner's stand-in)
the colouring (the picture is sepia; hair and eye colours are readings of its tones)
the cameo brooch, the hoop earrings and the wedding ring (no jewellery is modelled on the town's figures)
the dress's pin-tucked bodice, its buttons and its leg-of-mutton sleeves (the lady's body keeps its own jacket, coloured as hers)

stand_in.label: STAND-IN, NOT SARAH GREY
stand_in.card_note: No photograph of Sarah Grey is known. This is a stand-in the project's owner chose as her likeness: a sepia portrait of a woman in a dark day dress with a lace collar and a cameo brooch, her hair drawn up to a knot on the crown. Its sitter is not recorded. Her face, hair and dress are the model's guide; it is not Sarah Grey.

read_by_eye.basis: Read by eye from the same picture, on axes the marks cannot measure from one near-frontal view or read wrongly through the render's painting: a nose of ordinary width and thin lips (her cheekbones, cheeks and jowls are now fitted from the sheet's front view instead). Her lower lip is thin in both its volume (lip_lower) and its height (lip_lower_height, MakeHuman's own lower-lip height target, added as a rest axis for this: the volume target alone left the painted lip as tall as before), and the tip of her nose is level, not turned up (nose_tip 0: the marks had turned it up, showing the nostrils, which the picture does not). Those three are HELD where they are read (`hold`), not fitted; the rest are priors the marks move. Owner, 2026-11-13: "she has finer features", "she has a much more diminutive chin", "you need to trace it".

card._doc: What the person's card shows (T-3413, T-3478): `portrait` is cut from the copy at `portrait_from_scan_px` and scaled to `size_px` by tools/cut_portrait.py (a stand-in's label burned on it); `model` is tools/portrait_still.mjs's render of the fitted face on `body`, turned to the fit's yaw, dressed as humans.js dresses the person in town.

likeness.hair_tone_basis: The stand-in portrait is sepia: her hair reads a light-to-mid brown with paler streaks through it, drawn a light brown going grey for that and her 54 years; the owner's turnaround sheet of her (2026-11-13, in colour) shows the same, an ash brown with grey and fair streaks, worn up in a full knot on the crown, and her eyes a blue-grey. Colours of a stand-in, not a record.

dress.worn: dark brown day dress with a white lace collar, as the stand-in portrait

likeness._doc: What the figure takes from the stand-in, for tools/prairie_people.py: hair drawn up to a knot on the crown and its colour (human-hair-styles.js), complexion, and the dress's colour on the lady's body, whose white shirtwaist collar and lace jabot stand for the portrait's high lace collar. Reconstructed readings of a sepia picture.

build.basis: Read by eye from the stand-in portrait (owner, 2026-11-12: "their build match is important"): a woman of full, sturdy build, broad in the shoulders and full in the bust and waist under a fitted bodice. A reading of a seated three-quarter portrait, not a measurement.

drawn_age.basis: Drawn at the age the stand-in portrait shows (about 45), not her recorded age of 54 in 1904, so the face matches the picture the owner chose ("their faces must match exactly"). A reading by eye of an undated picture; the record's age is unchanged.

axes_note: chin_prominence, prognathism and nose_depth move the face toward or away from a camera that looks at it nearly square, so one near-frontal picture does not measure them; they are read here from the side view in `fit_views` (T-3553, 2026-11-13).

trace.basis: The per-vertex trace (tools/trace_portrait_face.py) is withdrawn (owner, 2026-11-13: "her jaw is ragged and her nose is bad"): spot moves made where one view disagreed with the face fitted from the other left lumps (a pout beside the mouth, a stepped jaw). Her side view (`profile`, the owner's turnaround sheet, 2026-11-13: "These might help") and the sheet's square-on front view (owner: "her cheeks are seen well in the face on view") are now fitted together with the portrait (`fit_views`), so the nose's length and how far it stands out, the small chin and the line under the jaw come from one smooth face.

profile._doc: Sheet pixels. silhouette_px: the face's line against the sheet's white ground, from the forehead to the neck, every second pixel of its outline; marks_px: MediaPipe Face Landmarker points on the side view (the visible eye's corners and lids, the lips' meeting); tragus_px read by eye, with the skin vertex the render draws there (tragus_kit_vertex) (tools/trace_portrait_profile.py).

fit_views._doc: T-3553: the axes are fitted to these pictures of the same stand-in at once, each with its own camera (tools/fit_portrait_face.py fit_views): `fronts`, MediaPipe Face Landmarker points (478, sheet pixels) on another front picture; `profile`, the side view of trace.profile (its visible eye's outer corner and lids and the lips' meeting place a side camera turned near render_yaw_deg, its nod free; its silhouette is matched by the face's own outline from that side, from the brow down `to` the neck or, under a beard, to just below the nose; `lips: height` keeps only the lips' height where a moustache hangs in front of them; `camera_sigma_deg` holds the side camera near the turn read by eye, not tipped). `extended_limits` lets an axis pass MakeHuman's +-1 where the side view asks for more. `head_shape_option` and `side_outline` ([mesh vertex, silhouette point] pairs) are what a full closest-point search over every head outline found (written by tools/fit_portrait_face.py --find-outline, 2026-11-13); the fit solves once on them, so every numpy build lands it alike and the check stays quick.
